analysis: This batch contains only documentation and changelog changes. changelog.d/watchdog-rearm-after-failed-relaunch.md (new, lines 1-3) says restart/update now re-arm the crash-recovery watchdog when the old instance has drained and stopped but the relaunch (loadService) fails. The drain-timeout fence is unchanged. docs/provider/cli-reference.md head ~179-185 documents this and points to provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/ServiceDrain+Recovery.swift (ServiceDrain.relaunchDrainedProvider), which is not supplied. Relevant threats: T-043 (the watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable binary) and T-053 (stale authorization across connection change). Re-arming recovery after a failed relaunch means the watchdog may relaunch the provider. Because the relaunched process must still obtain fresh authorization, no new trust grant appears in this batch. Logout (cli-reference base 450-456) relies on recovery staying disabled while it holds the lifecycle lease. The next pass must verify three things in the Swift source: (1) logout and stop paths never call the new re-arm (only restart and update do); (2) re-arm happens only after the old process exit is confirmed and is not applied when the drain times out; (3) re-arm respects provider.auto_restart and the lifecycle lease, so it cannot race a concurrent logout or stop. No source code was provided, so the security conclusion is limited to documentation.
